stories.title: Dwight Capital Provides $24M Refi on New Jersey Multifamily Building
stories.excerpt: New Jersey developer Fadi Samaan has landed $23.5 million of U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)-backed debt to refinance a multifamily complex in Passaic, NJ., Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Capital supplied the HUD 223(f) loan on the 104-unit Station at Passaic Phase II development, completed in 2024. The deal, which was originated by Dwight Capital’s Jonathan Pomper and Noah Greenwald, closed nearly a year to the date of a $27.7 million HUD 223(f) loan the private lender executed for the adjacent 104-unit Station at Passaic Phase I property in August 2025. Loan proceeds will be used to retire existing debt, establish a replacement reserve account for funding future capital improvements and return equity built up during the construction and lease-up stages, according to Dwight. “Station at Passaic’s location on the NJ Transit line into Manhattan drives strong renter demand from both New York City and other New Jersey submarkets,” Pomper said in a statement. “With tight vacancy, limited new supply, and neighborhood amenities like the on-site restaurant and grocery store, the property is well positioned to meet that demand as reflected in Phase I’s strong lease-up and the natural progression to Phase II.” Located at 99 Passaic Street 14 miles west of Midtown Manhattan, Station at Passaic Phase II consists of two five-story apartment buildings with a unit mix of eight one-bedroom and 96 two-bedroom units. The property also features 7,813 square feet of retail space that includes a Pachos Mini Market. Samaan said in a statement that the loan closing process with Dwight was “even smoother than the last” and credited them with “making even the most complex financing feel straightforward.” Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Dwight Capital closed $23.5M HUD 223(f) refi on 104-unit Station at Passaic Phase II, Passaic, NJ.
Phase I (104 units) refinanced Aug 2025 for $27.7M; Phase II mirrors strong lease-up trajectory.
Transit proximity to Manhattan drives renter demand from NYC and NJ submarkets.
stories.summary: Fadi Samaan's Station at Passaic Phase II, a 104-unit multifamily completed in 2024, secured a $23.5M HUD 223(f) refi from Dwight Capital to retire debt and return equity. The adjacent Phase I property closed a nearly identical $27.7M loan in August 2025. Both phases benefit from direct NJ Transit access to Manhattan, generating strong cross-submarket renter demand.
stories.impact: Successful consecutive refinancings on twin Phase I/II properties signal healthy lease-up and strong fundamentals in Passaic, NJ. Transit-oriented multifamily with NYC commute appeal shows durable demand; developers should prioritize similar NJ Transit-adjacent sites in underutilized submarkets facing Manhattanward outmigration pressure and price arbitrage.

stories.title: Prominent Austin Office Tower Trades for $208M
stories.excerpt: Cousins Properties Inc. has sold the One Eleven Congress office building in downtown Austin to Canyon Creek Real Estate. Cousins sold the One Eleven Congress office building for $208 million. Eastdil Secured brokered the sale. The Austin Business Journal reports building improvements may include modernizing common areas and possibly adding a tenant lounge. Other big transactions in Austin of late include Cousins’ purchase of the Sail Tower for $522 million in 2024, a deal that Eastdil served as exclusive adviser, and Brandywine’s sale of 405 Colorado to Hines earlier this month, another deal that involved Eastdil as Brandywine’s representative. Built in 1987, One Eleven Congress is part of the Central Business District’s older office buildings. At 503,344 square feet, the 30-story building is the seventh-largest office tower in Austin. As of June 2025, One Eleven Congress was 84% leased. The property is Canyon Creek’s first in Austin. The Fort Worth-based firm was formed in 2025. The post Prominent Austin Office Tower Trades for $208M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cousins Properties sold One Eleven Congress, 503k SF Austin office tower, to Canyon Creek for $208M.
84% leased as of June 2025; 1987-built property represents older CBD stock ripe for modernization.
Canyon Creek formed 2025, making this their first Austin acquisition; signals investor confidence in office value-add.
stories.summary: Cousins Properties divested the 503,344-square-foot One Eleven Congress office tower in downtown Austin to Canyon Creek Real Estate for $208M. The 30-story building, built in 1987 and the seventh-largest in Austin, was 84% leased as of June 2025. Canyon Creek, a Fort Worth-based firm formed in 2025, plans modernization of common areas and possible tenant lounge additions.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, office distress and ownership transition to newly formed, capital-backed buyer signals continued Austin office sector volatility. For multifamily developers: aging CBD office conversions to residential may emerge; monitor Canyon Creek's renovation roadmap and any near-term office vacancy leakage that could compete for young professional renters in downtown Austin submarkets.

stories.title: Link Logistics Acquires DFW, Austin Warehouses
stories.excerpt: Link Logistics purchased a two-building industrial portfolio totaling 352,396 square feet in Texas’ Dallas-Fort Worth and Austin metropolitan areas. The portfolio includes two infill industrial properties: a 291,285-square-foot warehouse property at 450 Airline Drive (shown) in Coppell, Texas, located within the DFW Airport submarket, and a 61,111-square-foot facility at 2401 Double Creek Drive in Austin’s Round Rock submarket. Both properties were 100% leased at the time of addition. These properties provide additional exposure to markets where population growth and business expansion continue to support demand for well-located logistics space and reinforce our conviction in Texas as a long-term growth market. Link Logistics has an established presence in both markets, with more than 30 million square feet of warehouse space across Dallas-Fort Worth and more than 7 million square feet across the Austin metro area. The transaction was brokered by Stream Realty Partners. The post Link Logistics Acquires DFW, Austin Warehouses appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Link Logistics acquired 352k SF industrial portfolio: 291k SF in Coppell (DFW) and 61k SF in Round Rock (Austin).
Both properties 100% leased at acquisition; located in infill logistics submarkets with strong population and business growth.
Link holds 30M+ SF in DFW, 7M+ SF in Austin metro; reinforces Texas as long-term growth conviction.
stories.summary: Link Logistics purchased a two-building industrial portfolio totaling 352,396 square feet across Texas: a 291,285-SF warehouse in Coppell within the DFW Airport submarket and a 61,111-SF facility in Austin's Round Rock submarket. Both properties were 100% leased at close. Link already operates 30+ million square feet across DFW and 7+ million square feet in Austin.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. However, the continued strength and in-fill acquisition activity in DFW and Austin industrial space reinforces these metros as primary job-growth and population-migration destinations. Industrial absorption signals sustained corporate/logistics presence, which sustains demand for workforce housing; multifamily developers should ensure pipeline aligns with DFW airport-corridor and Round Rock job corridors.

stories.title: EDENS Picks Up 179K-SF FW Retail Center
stories.excerpt: A 179,376-square-foot retail center in Fort Worth has traded hands. JLL represented the seller, Dunhill. The buyer was EDENS. The Village at Camp Bowie sits along Camp Bowie Boulevard. The property’s tenant roster features a mix of grocery, dining and service concepts, including Sprouts Farmers Market The center benefits from Fort Worth’s explosive growth trajectory as the nation’s 11th largest city and fifth fastest-growing large city in America. The area has experienced 9.7% population growth since 2020, supported by major developments including the $1.7 billion Westside Village mixed-use project, Walsh Ranch’s 7,200-acre master-planned community, and Edwards Ranch Riverhills, where 567 single-family homes with a median value of $1.9 million are under development. JLL Capital Market’s Sales and Advisory team representing the seller was led by Adam Howells, Chris Gerard, Michael Jankovich and Elizabeth Anne Casillas. The post EDENS Picks Up 179K-SF FW Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: EDENS acquired 179k SF Village at Camp Bowie retail center in Fort Worth from Dunhill.
Fort Worth: 11th largest US city, 5th fastest-growing large city; 9.7% population growth since 2020.
Surrounding developments: $1.7B Westside Village mixed-use, 7,200-acre Walsh Ranch, 567-home Edwards Ranch Riverhills ($1.9M median).
stories.summary: EDENS purchased the 179,376-square-foot Village at Camp Bowie retail center in Fort Worth, featuring Sprouts Farmers Market and a mix of grocery, dining, and service tenants. Fort Worth is the nation's 11th-largest city and fifth-fastest growing large city, with 9.7% population growth since 2020. Surrounding developments include the $1.7 billion Westside Village mixed-use project and Walsh Ranch's 7,200-acre master-planned community.
stories.impact: Fort Worth's explosive growth (9.7% since 2020) and massive pipeline of high-value residential developments (Westside Village, Walsh Ranch, Edwards Ranch Riverhills) indicate sustained population in-migration and household formation. Multifamily developers should prioritize infill and mixed-use opportunities near high-traffic retail corridors like Camp Bowie; proximity to EDENS-quality grocers and services signals strong renter demand and density appetite in this submarket.

stories.title: Kroger Taking Over Most of Shuttered Dunwoody Walmart Store
stories.excerpt: A Kroger Marketplace is taking over a former Walmart store near Perimeter Mall in Dunwoody. The Atlanta Business Chronicle reports that Kimco, the owner of Perimeter Village since 2022, worked out the deal with Kroger’s to take over 118,000 square feet of the 183,000 square foot building. Walmart vacated its space in 2024. The plan for the super-sized market includes a drive-thru pharmacy and fuel station, as well as a Starbucks coffee counter and specialty departments such as baby apparel and kitchenware. Located at Ashford Dunwoody Road and Meadow Lane, the shopping center dates back to the 1990s. Current retail tenants include Carter’s, DSW, Hobby Lobby, Perimeter Bottle Shop and World Market, along with several restaurants and service-based establishments. Kroger has not said when it plans to open the new store. It’s also not clear what Kimco’s plans are for the remaining space in the former Walmart building. The post Kroger Taking Over Most of Shuttered Dunwoody Walmart Store appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kroger Marketplace taking over 118k SF of shuttered 183k SF former Walmart store in Dunwoody, Atlanta.
Kimco owns Perimeter Village since 2022; Walmart vacated 2024; Kroger plans pharmacy, fuel, Starbucks.
Perimeter Mall submarket anchored by Carter's, DSW, Hobby Lobby, World Market, and service/dining tenants.
stories.summary: Kroger Marketplace is leasing 118,000 square feet of a 183,000-square-foot former Walmart store in Dunwoody near Perimeter Mall in Atlanta, vacated in 2024. Kimco, which acquired Perimeter Village in 2022, brokered the deal. The Kroger will include a drive-thru pharmacy, fuel station, Starbucks, and specialty departments. No opening timeline announced; plans for remaining space unclear.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance, but signals healthy retail backfill in the Perimeter submarket. Loss of Walmart and replacement with Kroger Marketplace (higher-quality grocer) could uplift nearby residential appeal; multifamily developers should monitor if Kimco converts remaining vacant space to mixed-use or office, which could alter local renter demographics and demand profile in this north Atlanta submarkets.

stories.title: Waterton Acquires Franklin Apartments at Discount
stories.excerpt: Waterton paid $128.11 million for Franklin’s Wyndchase Aspen Grove development, a high price to pay for a rental community. Despite the sale price, the Nashville Business Journal reports that the seller, Berkshire Residential Investments, lost money on the deal. Berkshire paid $138.1 million for the apartment community in 2019. Built in 1997, Wyndchase Aspen Grove sits on 60 acres at 3100 Aspen Grove Dr. in Franklin, south of Nashville. The rental community offers 560 units with one-, two- or three-bedrooms, including townhome-style options, across multiple buildings. Amenities at Wyndchase include a clubhouse with a game room, fitness center, two pools and outdoor dining and grilling stations. “Wyndchase Aspen Grove represents a highly differentiated product with strong value add upside and an opportunity to provide an updated and relatively attainable rental option,” said Waterton’s Casey Mog. Founded in 1995, Waterton Residential LLC has $10 billion in real estate assets across 25 markets,. The post Waterton Acquires Franklin Apartments at Discount appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Waterton acquired Wyndchase Aspen Grove (560 units, 60 acres, Franklin TN) for $128.11M; seller lost $10M from 2019.
Built 1997; mix of 1/2/3-bed units including townhome-style; amenities: clubhouse, fitness, two pools.
Waterton ($10B AUM, 25 markets) sees strong value-add and "attainable rental option" upside.
stories.summary: Waterton Residential paid $128.11M for Wyndchase Aspen Grove, a 560-unit, 60-acre apartment community in Franklin, south of Nashville. The seller, Berkshire Residential Investments, lost money on the transaction, having paid $138.1M in 2019. Built in 1997, the community offers one-, two-, and three-bedroom units plus townhome-style options with a clubhouse, fitness center, two pools, and outdoor amenities.
stories.impact: Distressed value-add opportunity in Franklin submarket signals seller pressure and cap-rate expansion since 2019, likely driven by rising construction costs and rate environment. Waterton's willingness to underwrite at discount indicates market confidence in Nashville's workforce-housing demand and feasibility to renovate aging product. Franklin's continued residential growth supports multifamily redevelopment; developers should scout similar early-2000s suburban communities with renovation-friendly unit layouts and strong location fundamentals.

stories.title: AvalonBay Communities, Equity Residential Merger Rebrands as Vivmark Residential
stories.excerpt: A new company brings a new name. Two months after multifamily giants AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential merged to form one of the country’s largest real estate companies — the total enterprise value is calculated at $71 billion — the two firms announced Friday that their new company will be called Vivmark Residential. The new firm, which is a publicly traded real estate investment trust (REIT), will hold the New York Stock Exchange ticker symbol VMRK. “The name Vivmark Residential reflects what we are building — a company determined to set a new standard for the experience of home,” said Benjamin Schall, CEO of AvalonBay Communities and the new CEO of the combined entity. The new name combines two words — Viv, from the Latin word “vivere,” or “to live fully,” and the English word “mark,” meaning “quality, distinction, and lasting impact,” according to a release from AvalonBay. “Vivmark Residential is built from the exceptional foundations that AvalonBay and Equity Residential have each spent more than 30 years establishing as trusted leaders,” added Schall. Vivmark Residential will take control of the residential REIT landscape as the new biggest player on the block. The combined entity will hold a portfolio of more than 180,000 rental apartments across 600 distinct apartment communities and assets, with another 10,800 units and $4.4 billion of development in its construction pipeline. AvalonBay stock currently trades at $187 per share, as of Friday morning, down 2 percent over the last five days, while Equity Residential stock trades at $67 per share, also down 2 percent in the last week. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2026. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential merger completed; combined entity rebrands as Vivmark Residential.
Total enterprise value: $71 billion; new NYSE ticker VMRK; Benjamin Schall (AvalonBay CEO) leads combined firm.
Name blends Latin 'vivere' (to live fully) and 'mark' (quality, distinction, lasting impact).
stories.summary: Two months after AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential merged to form a $71 billion enterprise value company, the combined entity announced its new name: Vivmark Residential. The publicly traded REIT will trade on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker VMRK, with Benjamin Schall serving as CEO. The name combines 'Viv' from the Latin 'vivere' (to live fully) and 'mark' (quality and distinction).
stories.impact: Creation of a $71B multifamily REIT consolidates significant capital, platform, and operating leverage across 25+ markets. Vivmark's scale enhances acquisition speed, cost of capital, and development velocity, raising competitive bar for mid-size and regional developers. Watch for aggressive deployment into high-barrier-to-entry markets and value-add portfolios; smaller developers should seek niche (workforce housing, secondary markets, specialized product) where Vivmark may lack focus or face regulatory scrutiny on concentration.

stories.title: Tom Giordano of Suffolk Construction: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: From a young age, Tom Giordano, general manager of New York for Suffolk Construction, had one goal. That was to follow in his uncle’s footsteps and become a lawyer to benefit his community. After going from litigation to representing general contractors, developers and design professionals on legal matters, he joined Morse Diesel Construction in 1999, then Bovis Lend Lease in 2004 as general counsel. For the last four and a half years, he has been managing the New York office of Suffolk Construction, working in a non-legal executive role. Giordano is responsible for enhancing the company’s internal organization processes and its infrastructure, as well as ensuring Suffolk is in a strong position to grow and expand construction management projects in the metro area — which for the firm includes New York City, Westchester and Long Island — in the hospitality, health care and residential spaces. Commercial Observer caught up with Giordano in July to discuss what projects Suffolk has been working on recently, notable market trends in New York City’s construction industry, and how the firm takes a project from an idea to reality. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What is the mission of Suffolk Construction in New York? Tom Giordano: Our mission is pretty simple. We want New York to be similar to what Suffolk is nationally. We want to be not necessarily the biggest, but the best construction management firm in the New York metro area, and deliver the Suffolk culture here. We’ve had a New York presence for 13 years, but we’ve really gotten a significant amount of traction over the last five and a half years. We’ve grown significantly. When I started, we were probably doing $350 million a year in revenue. Now we’re doing $1.3 billion, with a real look at $2 billion a year in the next two years. bullets: Tom Giordano, GM of Suffolk Construction New York, leads NYC, Westchester, Long Island residential/hospitality/healthcare.
Suffolk enhancing internal processes and infrastructure to expand construction management in three-state metro region.
Giordano transitioned from legal (Bovis Lend Lease GC 2004) to operations; 4.5 years in current role.
stories.summary: Tom Giordano, general manager of New York for Suffolk Construction, oversees the firm's operations across NYC, Westchester, and Long Island in hospitality, healthcare, and residential sectors. Previously general counsel at Bovis Lend Lease and before that with Morse Diesel, Giordano has spent the last four and a half years in his current non-legal executive role, focused on enhancing internal processes and infrastructure to support expansion of construction management projects.
stories.impact: Minimal material impact on market fundamentals. Profile signals Suffolk's intention to build organizational depth and operational efficiency in Northeast multifamily construction. Developers underwriting projects in tri-state should assess Suffolk's availability and capacity; his shift from legal to operations may indicate firm's move toward higher-margin, larger-scale residential development delivery versus traditional GC work.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs Group Deploys $116M for Syracuse Affordable Housing Overhaul
stories.excerpt: Goldman Sachs has provided a $116 million construction loan as part of an overall $269 million financing package to facilitate the redevelopment of a long-standing Syracuse affordable housing complex, Commercial Observer can first report. The investment bank’s Urban Investment Group provided the loan on BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group’s transformation of the Parkside Commons Section 8-backed housing complex in Syracuse’s East Side neighborhood. The project will feature 393 apartments designated as affordable through a combination of newly constructed and renovated units. “Parkside Commons represents a significant investment in not only the preservation but also the creation of affordable housing in Syracuse,” Asahi Pompey, chair of the Urban Investment Group at Goldman Sachs, said in a statement. “We are proud to partner with New York State, BFC Partners, and SAA Canopy Group to deliver quality homes that will serve Syracuse families for years to come.” The $269 million financing package also includes federal and state Low-Income Housing Tax Credits slated to raise $88 million and $13.6 million, respectively. The remainder of the funds will derive from interest earnings on tax-exempt bond proceeds for the development and interim project income generated during construction, according to BFC. BFC and SAA acquired the 15-acre property on 1901 East Fayette Street in late 2024 from a partnership connected to developer Stephen Ross, the Syracuse Post-Standard reported at the time. The 10-building complex, constructed in the mid-20th century, had previously faced security and crime challenges, according to the Post-Standard. Loan proceeds will be used for BFC and SAA Canopy to renovate six of the current buildings at the complex and build two new ones, which will have enough space to relocate all current residents from the four oldest structures slated for demolition The site of the demolished buildings will later be used for additional housing in a later developm
bullets: Goldman Sachs Urban Investment Group deployed $116M construction loan on $269M total financing for Parkside Commons, Syracuse.
BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group redeveloping Section 8 complex; 393 apartments (new + renovated) preserved as affordable.
Project on East Side neighborhood; funded with federal/state Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and HUD/state subsidy.
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs' Urban Investment Group provided a $116M construction loan as part of a $269M financing package for Parkside Commons, a Section 8-backed affordable housing complex in Syracuse's East Side neighborhood. BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group are transforming the project into 393 preserved and newly constructed affordable apartments. The financing also includes federal and state Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and HUD/state subsidies.
stories.impact: Demonstrates continued appetite from large capital (Goldman Sachs) for affordable/tax-credit multifamily in secondary markets. Syracuse's population and income base may constrain rent-growth; however, Goldman's conviction signals long-term value in preservation + renovation of aging Section 8 stock with subsidy backstop. Developers in Rust Belt/secondary metros should explore similar public-private partnerships combining LIHTC, state bonds, and institutional construction capital for obsolete affordable inventories.

stories.title: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission Takes 39K SF at AmTrustRE’s 250 Broadway
stories.excerpt: This TLC wasn’t exactly chasing waterfalls, just a new office. The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission is relocating to AmTrustRE’s 250 Broadway across the street from City Hall Park in Manhattan’s Financial District, the property owner announced Thursday. The TLC is relocating its headquarters from another FiDi office at 33 Beaver Street and will occupy 39,000 square feet on the entire fourth floor and a portion of the fifth floor of its new building. The space includes a variety of private offices, conference rooms and a hearing room for public proceedings, according to AmTrustRE. The agency is expected to move into 250 Broadway in the first quarter of 2027. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in the Financial District was $60.61 per square foot during the first quarter, according to Colliers data. AmTrustRE was represented in-house by Anne Holker, and by Brad Gerla, Michael Rizzo and Alex Benisatto from CBRE. The tenant was represented by Gus Field from Cushman & Wakefield. The brokers did not immediately respond to requests for comment. “The Financial District remains one of Downtown Manhattan’s most sought-after office markets, and this lease underscores the strong demand we’re continuing to see for high-quality workplace environments in the neighborhood,” Holker said in a statement announcing the lease. “We’re pleased to welcome TLC to 250 Broadway, where they join a dynamic mix of public and private sector tenants. We look forward to supporting their success and building a long-term tenancy.” This deal brings 250 Broadway, a 31-story, 648,000-square-foot office tower, to 90 percent leased. Other tenants in the building include coworking company WeWork, law firm Rose & Rose, and academic publishing company IGI. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission leasing 39k SF (4th floor + partial 5th) at AmTrustRE's 250 Broadway, FiDi.
Relocating from 33 Beaver Street; move-in Q1 2027; space includes offices, conference rooms, public hearing room.
FiDi avg asking rent Q1 2025: $60.61/SF; lease terms and rent not disclosed.
stories.summary: The NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission is relocating its headquarters to 250 Broadway in Manhattan's Financial District, leasing 39,000 square feet across the entire fourth floor and a portion of the fifth floor. The agency is moving from its current office at 33 Beaver Street and will occupy space with private offices, conference rooms, and a public hearing room. Expected occupancy is Q1 2027; lease terms and rent were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, TLC relocation signals landlord confidence in FiDi office fundamentals and AmTrustRE's ability to attract government tenancy. For multifamily developers: government leasing activity stabilizes office market and anchors Financial District foot traffic and retail/services, which supports nearby residential demand. Monitor whether additional municipal tenants follow TLC to 250 Broadway or other FiDi properties; sustained government occupancy could underpin demand for workforce/young professional housing in lower Manhattan submarkets.
